newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine wins Iran orders, no fuel deliveries yet.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine wins Iran orders, no fuel deliveries yet.

text.p: Ukraine has won Iranian industrial orders worth $52 million after a visit by a senior Tehran delegation but Ukraine's hopes of buying Iranian energy to ease its dependence on Russian fuel are as far away as ever.
Valery Kazakov, Ukraine's Deputy Minister for Machine Building, the Military Complex and Conversion, said cooperation between the two states was at "the highest level".
"The main achievement is that Ukraine has won the chance of selling its technologies," he told reporters at the weekend.
The Iranian delegation, headed by Industry Minister Mohammad Reza Nematzadeh, spent a week in Ukraine, visiting industrial cities in the east of the former Soviet republic.
Tehran ordered metallurgy products worth $26.5 million and railway locomotives and carriages worth $25.5 million.
Kiev has long said it wants to buy Iranian oil and gas to ease its dependency on Russian imports, but Ukrainian officials said a shortage of pipelines and oil terminals meant no deal has been signed.

"Ukraine is very intrested in Iranian energy supplies, but it should be very careful dealing with the Iranians," Oleksei Haran, head of analytical centre of the Den daily newspaper, told Reuters on Sunday.
"Ukraine is not a western European country, which can simply ignore U.S. warnings...but Iran is still an option."
The United States, which is considered by Ukraine as a "strategic partner", says Tehran is sponsoring terrorism and seeking to acquire weapons of mass destruction.
Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko said last week that Ukraine would not violate any international norms. "There is too much speculation around (on ties with Iran)," he said.
Diplomatic sources said Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani would visit Ukraine in the second half of 1997 to discuss the possible routes of energy supplies with President Leonid Kuchma.
Kiev is also involved in a complicated barter deal with Tehran under which Turkmenistan supplies gas to Ukraine, Ukraine pays Iran and Iran supplies goods to Turkmenistan.

Ukraine won a tender in Iran last year to convert a helicopter plant in the city of Esfahan into a plant building planes. Kiev will produce 10 Antonov-140 short-haul turbo-prop planes there a year, each with capacity for 52 passengers.
